title: Module-object and ringed-site derived internal Hom agree
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its pro-étale site taken small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and put $B=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], a commutative ring object of abelian sheaves with the sheafified pointwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; write $B_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for its section-ring sheaf. Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of $B$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(B_{\mathrm{sec}})$ the category of sheaves of $B_{\mathrm{sec}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $F:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal M$ the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which leaves underlying abelian sheaves, sections and morphisms unchanged. Let $D(F)$ be its termwise extension to the ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and identify the K-flat derived relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] with the ordinary ringed-site K-flat derived tensor through the comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Let $\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A}_B$ be the derived internal Hom of $D(\mathcal A)$, defined as the right adjoint of this derived relative tensor in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and let $R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}$ be the functorial K-injective sheaf-Hom model of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for all $K,N\in D(\mathcal A)$ there are isomorphisms
$$D(F)\bigl(\operatorname{RHom}_{B}^{\mathcal A}(K,N)\bigr)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}(D(F)K,D(F)N),$$
natural in $K$ (contravariantly) and $N$, which carry the evaluation morphism $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_B\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A}_B(K,N)\to N$, transported by $D(F)$ and the tensor comparison, to the ringed-site evaluation $D(F)K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}(D(F)K,D(F)N)\to D(F)N$. For every object $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, restricting these isomorphisms to the slice site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives the corresponding isomorphisms for the ring object $B|_U$ and its section-ring sheaf.

proof.text: Put $E=D(F)$ and $U=D(F^{-1})$. Exactness and K-flatness preservation follow from the internal-section tensor comparison. Localizing the exact equivalence and its inverse gives $E\dashv U$ with invertible unit and counit, by the exact derived adjunction. Write $T,T_0$ for the native internal and ringed derived tensors.

The small ringed site has a functorial flat cover $C\to1$. On internal modules its transport is $F^{-1}CF\to F^{-1}F\cong1$; exactness preserves epimorphisms and the tensor comparison reflects flatness. For an internal complex $K$, a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to FK$ gives $F^{-1}P\to F^{-1}FK\cong K$, again a K-flat resolution by reflection. Apply the normalized exact tensor-functor lemma to $F$, which is an exact symmetric monoidal left adjoint preserving flats and K-flat complexes. It gives $t:E(T(K,L))\cong T_0(EK,EL)$ with the prescribed total-complex normalization and native associator/unit equations. The separate derived-braiding lemma applies because the ordinary section-action comparison respects symmetry; it gives the native Koszul equation for this same $t$.

proof.text: The native ringed tensor and K-injective Hom admit the normalized closed structure $S$ and representative models $T_0$ by the ringed derived tensor-Hom adjunction. Its native Koszul symmetry is the one in the native tensor lemma. On internal modules use the given native derived tensor-Hom adjunction; symmetry writes both evaluations with Hom first.

Apply the closed scalar Hom comparison to $E\dashv U$ and $t$, at $N=EL$. Compose its isomorphism $UH(EK,EL)\cong H_{\mathcal A}(K,UEL)$ with $H_{\mathcal A}(1,\eta_L^{-1})$, calling the result $b$. Then $\theta=\varepsilon_{H(EK,EL)}\circ E(b^{-1})$. Its naturality and evaluation equation follow from that comparison: the triangle identities cancel the inserted unit and counit. Step 2 symmetry gives the displayed tensor order.

For every $U\in X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, its slice is small and $(B|_U)_{\rm sec}=B_{\rm sec}|_U$ sectionwise. Apply Steps 1–4 on this site, obtaining $t_U,\theta^U$ for the native local module-object structures specified in the slice comparison definition. Exact restriction gives $E_U r_{\mathcal A}\cong rE$. Thus this construction covers all local derived objects.

Choose normalized ringed slice data $d$; its evaluation equation holds by slice evaluation coherence. Let $\rho:rH\cong H_U(r,r)$ be its Hom comparison. Full faithfulness of $E_U$ uniquely lifts $(\theta^U)^{-1}\rho\,r\theta$ to $r_U$. This is the required restriction square. Only this single-slice square is asserted; no compatibility along successive slices $V\to U$ is claimed or needed.

This is the human's 2026-10-21 re-split, reopened after Q63's landing because that landing added no new node. Ledger line 19694 shows Q63 was the last merge, so the base is the live Q63 text. Compared with live, the statement, stmt_deps and steps 1 and 3-6 are unchanged. Only Step 2, proof_deps and split_report changed. The proof is 2645 characters in 6 steps (none over 783). The old 6739-character proof's arguments all reappear: the tensor comparison is now Step 2 plus the two new nodes; the adjunction and Yoneda steps are lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction and lem-sfb-closed-scalar-hom-comparison; the slice step is def-sfb-internal-slice-derived-hom-comparison plus the two slice nodes. The base Step 2's invertibility, Koszul and unit sentences became the two new nodes, and the flat-cover transport is now written out. Step 2 checks: lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover applies because the site is small. F^-1CF is flat because lem-pe reflects flatness, and F^-1P is K-flat by the same reflection. lem-pe gives the other hypotheses of the new nodes: exact, strong monoidal (the c orientation), flat and K-flat preservation, and symmetry. Closedness and the Grothendieck property of the module-object category follow elementarily from the equivalence. Normalization node: all types check (normalization square, e, associator, unitors). It is true: on K-flat pairs t is a composite of isomorphisms; 1[0] is itself K-flat; the left-adjoint hypothesis lets F commute with the infinite sums of the total tensor. Tested on the identity functor, -⊗Q: Ab→Q-Vect (exact but not an equivalence) and zero categories; Z→Z/2 is excluded as non-exact. Braiding node: true, because F is additive (so it keeps the (-1)^pq signs) and τ commutes with the exchanges summand by summand; odd-degree rank-one complexes give -1 on both sides. Neither new node restates the item. The duplicate candidates are not duplicates: new-lem-kun-exact-monoidal-equivalence-derived is existential, needs an equivalence with monoidal counit, uses the étale def-kun-derived-tensor and does not name pur's t; lem-sfb-ringed-derived-tensor-lift covers only RingedTensorEdges; lem-pur-derived-tensor-comparison gives t without invertibility or coherence. Both new nodes have B1-B9 and four kinds of logged searches. A DFS over both new nodes' dependencies finds no cycle. No SGA is cited. Sources checked: Stacks sites-cohomology 0FPQ (l.12936) and 0FPT (l.13136), both with omitted proofs, so the agent-extraction label is right; blueprint main-20261015 lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves.proof.md.
